basis: Nonsyndromic inherited hearing loss; no extra-auditory disease.
Myeloid malignancy affecting marrow and blood cells, with dysplasia and cytopenias.
Neoplasm arising in the jejunum; lymphoma is only one possible subtype.
Malignant fibroblastic neoplasm arising in the kidney.
Immune-mediated destructive inflammation of muscle fascia; skin lesions are variable without an established frequency of at least 30%.
Primary breast carcinoma; breast has no axis.
Carcinoma arising in nasopharyngeal epithelium; nasopharynx belongs to the airway axis. EBV association alone does not make carcinoma an infection.
Inflammation of renal tissue; this umbrella includes multiple mechanisms, so immune mediation is not universal.
Telomere-related pulmonary fibrosis and marrow failure define the syndrome; hepatic failure and nodular regenerative hyperplasia reported in 1/1 assessed, with limited sampling.
Functional disorder of neutrophils, impairing innate immune defense; organ infections vary across subtypes.
Damage to multiple separate peripheral nerves; associated systemic diseases are distinct diagnoses and do not establish a universal immune mechanism.
Medication-induced neurologic movement disorder characterized by motor restlessness.
Demyelinating sensorimotor neuropathy; structural scoliosis in 12/13 supports musculoskeletal involvement. Ocular abnormalities are occasional.
GH resistance with IGF-I deficiency; skeletal growth impairment and delayed maturation are nearly universal; microdontia and tooth agenesis occur in 80-99%.
Inherited anticoagulant protein deficiency causing hypercoagulability; thromboses are separate events, and warfarin skin necrosis is treatment-related.
Infection of the vagina establishes the infectious mechanism axis; the reproductive site has no organ axis.
Vascular neoplasm arising within the cerebral hemisphere, defining both cerebral and blood-vessel involvement.
Inherited cerebral small-vessel disease causing hemorrhage and porencephaly; esotropia alone does not establish direct ocular tissue damage.
Recurrent subcutaneous, intestinal and upper-airway edema define this syndrome. F12-associated edema is bradykinin-mediated, without an established immune mechanism.
Developmental brain malformations and neurodevelopmental impairment define the syndrome; urinary tract defects occur in 30-79%. Craniosynostosis is occasional.
Inherited brain iron metabolism disorder with neurodegeneration; optic atrophy in 20/23 directly damages vision. Incontinence and dysphagia reflect neurologic dysfunction.
Progressive corticospinal disease with frequent peripheral axonal neuropathy; cardiomyopathy, arrhythmia and diabetes are occasional, below 30%.
Genetic developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; optic atrophy in 1/1 supports ocular involvement, although evidence is limited to one annotated patient.
Inherited rod-cone retinal degeneration; cataracts and other documented manifestations remain within the ocular axis.
Ovarian teratoma containing thyroid tissue; ovarian origin has no axis. Thyrotoxicosis occurs in fewer than 10% and does not support routine endocrine involvement.
